title: To amend title 28, United States Code, to add Flagstaff and Yuma to the list of locations in which court shall be held in the judicial district for the State of Arizona.
official_summary: This bill adds Flagstaff and Yuma to the list of locations where court must be held in the U.S. District of Arizona.

summary.headline: A 2019 law adds Flagstaff and Yuma to the places where federal court must be held in Arizona's federal district.
summary.what_it_does: This law changes the federal court code so that Flagstaff and Yuma are listed among the locations where the U.S. District Court for Arizona must hold court. Before this change, those two cities were not on that list. The summary does not say how many court sessions will be held there or what changes in court operations.

who_it_affects.group: People with federal cases in northern and western Arizona
who_it_affects.how: Federal court proceedings for people in the Flagstaff and Yuma areas may be held closer to home under the updated list of court locations.

who_it_affects.group: Federal court staff and judges in the Arizona district
who_it_affects.how: The court is required to hold court in Flagstaff and Yuma, which affects how sessions are scheduled in those cities.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted August 9, 2019; the summary does not list a separate effective date.
